candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current metformin contrast-media precautions by holding metformin in specified at-risk patients and restarting only after 48-hour renal reassessment confirms stability.

options.A: Continue metformin without interruption because the eGFR is above 30 mL/min/1.73 m²
options.B: Permanently discontinue metformin and convert the client to insulin
options.C: Hold metformin at or before the procedure, re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours later, and restart if renal function is stable
options.D: Double the metformin dose before contrast administration to maintain glycemic control

candidate.rationale: Current FDA-label information states that metformin should be discontinued at the time of, or before, iodinated contrast imaging in patients with an eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m². eGFR should be re-evaluated 48 hours after the procedure, and metformin may be restarted if renal function is stable.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For iodinated contrast imaging, patients taking metformin with eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m² should stop metformin at or before the procedure, have eGFR reassessed 48 hours later, and restart only if renal function is stable.
candidate.source_document_title: Metformin Hydrochloride Extended-Release Tablets — Full Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Dosage and Administration, Section 2.3 Discontinuation for Iodinated Contrast Imaging Procedures
candidate.stem: A client taking metformin has an eGFR of 45 mL/min/1.73 m² and is scheduled for an imaging procedure using intravascular iodinated contrast. Which plan is consistent with current prescribing information?
